method intersection(interval1: (int, int), interval2: (int, int)) returns (result: string)
    requires interval1.0 <= interval1.1 // start of interval1 is less than or equal to end
    requires interval2.0 <= interval2.1 // start of interval2 is less than or equal to end
    requires interval1.1 >= interval1.0 // interval1 is a closed interval
    requires interval2.1 >= interval2.0 // interval2 is a closed interval
    ensures result == "YES" || result == "NO" // result must be either "YES" or "NO"
    ensures (result == "YES" ==> (lengthOfIntersection(interval1, interval2) isPrime)) // if result is "YES", length is prime
    ensures (result == "NO" ==> !(lengthOfIntersection(interval1, interval2) isPrime)) // if result is "NO", length is not prime

method lengthOfIntersection(interval1: (int, int), interval2: (int, int)) returns (length: int)
    ensures length >= 0 // length of intersection cannot be negative
    ensures (length > 0 ==> (interval1.0 <= interval2.1 && interval2.0 <= interval1.1)) // intersection exists if length > 0
    ensures (length == 0 ==> (interval1.1 < interval2.0 || interval2.1 < interval1.0)) // no intersection if length is 0

function isPrime(n: int) : bool
    requires n >= 0 // n must be non-negative
    ensures (isPrime(n) ==> n > 1 && forall i: int :: 2 <= i < n ==> n % i != 0) // n is prime if greater than 1 and not divisible by any i
    ensures (!isPrime(n) ==> (n <= 1 || exists i: int :: 2 <= i < n && n % i == 0)) // not prime if less than or equal to 1 or divisible by some i
